champion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla
ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla

facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of a gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek
a diffuse, firm, non-tender mass measuring about 4 × 5 cm
extended from the infraorbital region superiorly to the lip commissure inferiorly, medially obliterating the nasal ala, and laterally approaching the preauricular area
well-defined vestibular swelling measuring 4 × 3 cm, extending from the distal aspect of the left canine to the second molar
Routine hematologic parameters were within normal limits
Contrast-enhanced CT of the head and neck showed a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion in the left premaxillary region
adjacent bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus
a provisional diagnosis of malignancy of the left maxilla was made
differential diagnosis included benign tumor, sarcoma, lymphoma, and melanoma
An incisional biopsy suggested myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia

concepts.preferred_label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the maxilla
concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek, along with the CT findings of a mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion and adjacent bony destruction, suggests a malignant process, with squamous cell carcinoma being a common type of cancer in this region.
The differential diagnosis included benign tumor, which is a possible explanation for the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.
Sarcoma is another type of cancer that could explain the patient's presentation and imaging findings, and it was included in the differential diagnosis.
Lymphoma is a possible explanation for the patient's symptoms and imaging findings, and it was included in the differential diagnosis.
The incisional biopsy suggested myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, which is an inflammatory condition that could explain the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.
Melanoma is a type of cancer that could explain the patient's presentation and imaging findings, and it was included in the differential diagnosis.
The patient's presentation of a gradually enlarging swelling of the left cheek, along with the CT findings, could also suggest a chronic inflammatory process.
Although there is no clear history of trauma, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings could potentially be explained by a traumatic injury to the maxilla.
